builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: OpenGray: a benchmark for evaluating the decisions of radiotherapy planning agents
summary: OpenGray replaces aggregate dose-only evaluation of radiotherapy planning agents with a benchmark of planning tasks with known correct decisions, including infeasible contradictions and feasible controls. It costs the effort of constructing verified ground-truth decisions and stored reference plans, and adds a domain-specific evaluation harness rather than model or serving overhead. After adoption, favorable headline accuracy can still conceal failures on contradiction recognition, hard-goal satisfaction, and missing stop or escalation actions.
rationale: The benchmark is clinically important and directly relevant to agent evaluation, but its assets, setting, and safety requirements are specialized to radiotherapy rather than immediately adoptable for most constrained-infrastructure AI production systems.
technique: Decision-focused benchmark for radiotherapy planning agents

claims.statement: OpenGray replaces aggregate dose-only evaluation of radiotherapy planning agents with a benchmark of planning tasks with known correct decisions, including infeasible contradictions and feasible controls. It costs the effort of constructing verified ground-truth decisions and stored reference plans, and adds a domain-specific evaluation harness rather than model or serving overhead. After adoption, favorable headline accuracy can still conceal failures on contradiction recognition, hard-goal satisfaction, and missing stop or escalation actions.

LLM-based systems with a commercial model achieved decision accuracies of 95.4% and 92.1%, yet escalated only 50% (95% CI, 25-75%) and 25% (10-40%) of overlap contradictions requiring arithmetic on anatomy.
